texts.small-study.warning:
Primary asymmetry test: Pustejovsky-Rodgers test
Result: evidence of small-study effects (p = 0.011)
Usable studies: 12
Estimate: -3.531 (95% CI -6.073 to -0.9878)

Funnel plot asymmetry can reflect publication bias, heterogeneity, study design, or chance.

Interpret the plots and tests together. No single result proves or rules out publication bias.

The ordinary Egger test is not selected for standardized mean differences because it can create effect-standard-error artifacts.

Analysis warnings:
- Observed standard-error range should be considered when interpreting asymmetry results; the exact range is reported in the analysis summary.
- Ordinary SMD Egger is a separate effect-SE artifact and is never an automatic primary method.
texts.small-study.data-eligibility:
Effect measure: Standardized mean difference (SMD)
Studies analyzed: 12
Confidence level: 95% confidence interval
Primary test: Pustejovsky-Rodgers test
Observed standard-error range: [0.10274717, 0.22556814]
texts.small-study.tests:
Pustejovsky-Rodgers test (primary)
  Studies: 12
  Result: Evidence of small-study effects (p = 0.011).
  Test statistic: -3.094
  Coefficient: -3.531 (SE 1.141; 95% CI -6.073 to -0.9878)
  Model: Pustejovsky-Rodgers independent two-group regression

Classical Egger test (additional)
  Studies: 12
  Result: Evidence of small-study effects (p = 0.014).
  Test statistic: -2.955
  Coefficient: -3.488 (SE 1.180; 95% CI -6.117 to -0.8575)
  Model: multiplicative Egger regression
texts.small-study.pooled-comparison:
Common effect
  Estimate: 0.4150
  95% confidence interval: 0.3259 to 0.5041

Random effects (REML)
  Estimate: 0.3627
  95% confidence interval: 0.2275 to 0.4980

These are model comparisons, not estimates corrected for publication bias.
texts.small-study.references:
1. Standardized-mean-difference asymmetry test: Pustejovsky, J. E., & Rodgers, M. A. (2019). Testing for funnel plot asymmetry of standardized mean differences. Research Synthesis Methods, 10(1), 57-71. doi:10.1002/jrsm.1332.
2. Egger regression test: Egger, M., Davey Smith, G., Schneider, M., & Minder, C. (1997). Bias in meta-analysis detected by a simple, graphical test. BMJ, 315(7109), 629-634. doi:10.1136/bmj.315.7109.629.
3. Funnel plot axis choice: Sterne, J. A. C., & Egger, M. (2001). Funnel plots for detecting bias in meta-analysis: Guidelines on choice of axis. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, 54(10), 1046-1055. doi:10.1016/S0895-4356(01)00377-8.
4. Contour-enhanced funnel plots: Peters, J. L., Sutton, A. J., Jones, D. R., Abrams, K. R., & Rushton, L. (2008). Contour-enhanced meta-analysis funnel plots help distinguish publication bias from other causes of asymmetry. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, 61(10), 991-996. doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2007.11.010.
5. Trim-and-fill method: Duval, S., & Tweedie, R. (2000). Trim and fill: A simple funnel-plot-based method of testing and adjusting for publication bias in meta-analysis. Biometrics, 56(2), 455-463. doi:10.1111/j.0006-341X.2000.00455.x.
6. Implementation reference: Viechtbauer, W. (2010). Conducting meta-analyses in R with the metafor package. Journal of Statistical Software, 36(3), 1-48. doi:10.18637/jss.v036.i03.
texts.small-study.method-details:
Pustejovsky-Rodgers test
  Package: meta 8.5-0
  Predictor: sqrt(1/n.e + 1/n.c)
  Weighting: inverse variance from native Pustejovsky standard errors
  Inference: t-based Pustejovsky regression test
  Degrees of freedom: 10.00
  Exact p-value: 0.0113711
  Call: meta::metacont(n.e, mean.e, sd.e, n.c, mean.c, sd.c, sm='SMD', common=TRUE, random=TRUE, method.tau='REML', level=0.95); meta::metabias(x=prepared.SMD.model, method.bias='Pustejovsky', k.min=10, level=0.95)

Classical Egger test
  Package: meta 8.5-0
  Predictor: SE
  Weighting: inverse variance
  Inference: t-based meta::metabias test
  Degrees of freedom: 10.00
  Exact p-value: 0.01441912
  Call: meta::metabias(x=prepared.meta.model, method.bias='Egger', k.min=10, level=0.95)
